item.title: Triage · First Five Minutes
item.description:
Reversing triage

Before decompiling: what format is it, what architecture, what runtime, and can this machine execute it? Preserve an original and analyze a copy.

1. Identify the file

Linux/WSL examples, when these standard utilities are available:

sha256sum challenge
file challenge
xxd -l 64 challenge
strings -a -n 5 challenge
strings -a -e l -n 5 challenge

-a scans all bytes; -n 5 sets minimum string length; GNU strings -e l selects 16-bit little-endian strings. A Windows strings implementation may use different flags. strings guide, xxd guide.

item.title: Ghidra Cheatsheet · From Strings to Check
item.description:
Ghidra cheatsheet

One useful route: import → confirm processor → analyze → success/failure string → xrefs → validator → types/constants → verified input. Menus and shortcuts can differ by release/keymap; use the action’s context menu or Help if a shortcut differs.

Annotated layout diagram, not a captured screenshot. Panels are conceptual and can be docked differently in your installation.

item.title: Ghidra Plugins · Built-ins & Offline Extras
item.description:
Ghidra plugins and offline extensions

Start with the supplied installation. Built-in analysis can cover most CTF reversing. External extensions are optional tools with their own compatibility and event-approval status. This page contains no AI/MCP assistant extensions.

1. Plugin, extension and script are different

Type Meaning Typical entry point
Built-in plugin Feature already bundled with Ghidra File → Configure in a tool; Window panels
Extension Extra packaged module, often Java Project Manager → File → Install Extensions
Script A local Java/Python automation file Window → Script Manager and script directories
Standalone companion Separate program operating on sample/output Its own executable and dependencies

Menu labels differ slightly across releases. A missing feature may only need enabling in the current tool configuration. Do not download a third-party package to obtain a panel already bundled with Ghidra.

item.title: Static Analysis · Bytes, Types & Control Flow
item.description:
Static analysis

Recover the exact computation, not just a readable-looking decompiler listing. The details that usually decide a solve are length, integer width, signedness, byte order and the order of transformations.

1. Work backward from the decisive check

Success message
  ← deciding branch
  ← comparison / aggregate result
  ← transformed input / expected table
  ← preprocessing and original input source

Trace all callers when preprocessing occurs outside the validator. fgets may preserve a newline; scanf("%s") stops at whitespace; read returns bytes and may not append NUL. A length check can reject an otherwise correct decoded string.

item.title: Dynamic Debugging · Break, Inspect, Dump
item.description:
Dynamic debugging

Ask a narrow question, stop at the relevant instruction, inspect exact bytes, then verify the original program. Use the challenge VM/runtime and keep an unmodified executable copy.

1. Choose the debugger

Binary Tool
Native Linux ELF GDB
Native Windows PE x64dbg / x32dbg matching bitness
Managed .NET dnSpyEx
Cross-platform Ghidra mapping Ghidra Debugger / optional sync with supported backend

A native debugger can inspect CLR runtime code, but dnSpyEx exposes managed methods, metadata and locals more directly. A decompiled address is not automatically a runtime address under ASLR.

item.title: Strings & Encodings · Preserve the Bytes
item.description:
Strings and encodings

Find the bytes, record their offset/length, decode the right layer, then confirm where the result is used. Readable output is a lead, not proof of the flag.

1. ASCII and wide strings

strings -a -n 4 -t x challenge
strings -a -e l -n 4 -t x challenge
strings -a -e b -n 4 -t x challenge

GNU strings: -t x prints file offsets in hex, -e l scans 16-bit little-endian characters, -e b 16-bit big-endian. Check implementation support before using flags. UTF-16LE strings commonly appear as 66 00 6c 00 61 00 67 00.

item.title: Crypto & Obfuscation · Identify, Model, Verify
item.description:
Crypto and obfuscation in reversing

Identify the actual operation from code and constants. A familiar constant is a clue; a complete state update and data flow make the identification credible.

1. Quick recognition

Pattern Candidate What to record
XOR same byte / periodic table Single/repeating XOR Key bytes, starting offset, period
Add/subtract index Position-dependent transform Truncation width, index origin
Rotate + XOR/add Custom byte/word mixing Width, count, order
0x811c9dc5, multiply 0x01000193 FNV-1a 32-bit candidate XOR-before-multiply vs after, width, seed
0x9e3779b9 with paired word rounds TEA/XTEA-like candidate Exact round equations and endian
256-element permutation + swaps RC4-like state KSA/PRGA, drop count, key
expand 32-byte k + add/xor/rotate ChaCha/Salsa family Variant, nonce/counter layout
S-box/table rounds AES or custom substitution Match full structure, mode/key/IV
Dispatch loop and bytecode PC Custom VM Opcode widths, state, semantics

Standard crypto can also be hidden behind library calls. Inspect call arguments before reimplementing it. The Python cookbook covers library-backed crypto where permitted; the downloads here use stdlib byte transforms.

item.title: .NET · dnSpyEx, Resources & IL
item.description:
.NET reversing

Confirm managed metadata → find entry/event handler → read validation → inspect resources/static initialization → verify IL when C# is unclear. A PE extension alone does not identify managed code.

1. Open the right thing

Use dnSpyEx for a managed executable or DLL. Check assembly/module metadata, references and namespaces. A native launcher may load a separate managed DLL; single-file or protected bundles may need extraction using the runtime’s actual packaging format.

item.title: Python Snippets · Byte Workbench & Check Models
item.description:
Offline Python reversing snippets

Download before the event, keep the model explicit and verify the forward transform. These command-line scripts use Python 3 standard library by default and make no network requests. They are separate from Ghidra’s script runtimes.

Downloads

  • byte_workbench.py: explicit input bytes, slicing, XOR, all single-byte candidates, byte rotates/add/subtract, word swaps, Base64/hex and ROT13.
  • solve_constraints.py: a documented reversible validator example with a forward assertion; optional --z3 solves the same model if that separate package is permitted and installed.

These tools implement stated transformations; they do not automatically infer an unknown algorithm or solve arbitrary binaries. Local --output paths write binary files and may replace an existing file, so choose distinct output names.
